title: Explicit Public Permutations for Key-Alternating Ciphers
summary: A t-round KAC can at best be close to t-wise independent; suitable public permutations exist, but an explicit construction attaining the nearly optimal closeness remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Explicitly construct fixed permutations $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ for a key-alternating cipher (KAC) that are public and known to the adversary and, with only the round keys $s_i$ providing secret randomness, give the cipher the nearly optimal pointwise closeness to $t$-wise independence known to be achievable. A $t$-round KAC can at best be close to $t$-wise independent, while the known guarantee is purely existential: suitable permutations exist, and most choices work, but no explicit choice is provided.

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptographic primitive design focused on key-alternating ciphers and t-wise independence.
assumptions: The fixed permutations are public and known to the adversary
Only the round keys provide secret randomness
parameters: p_1,...,p_r: fixed permutations used by the KAC
s_i: round keys supplying secret randomness
t: round count and t-wise-independence level
scope.unresolved_remainder: An explicit choice of the fixed public KAC permutations that achieves the known nearly optimal pointwise closeness to t-wise independence.

progress.summary: The source presents an existential result: suitable fixed permutations exist and most choices work, but it does not explicitly construct them.
citation_labels: Tianren Liu et al., The $t$-wise Independence of Substitution-Permutation Networks
